'''Increased Range''' is an [[Engineering Blueprints|Engineering Blueprint]] for [[Frame Shift Drive|Frame Shift Drives]]. It increases the drive's optimized mass, allowing it to move the ship's mass more efficiently and generally increasing jump range.<ref name="inara">[https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/2/ Frame Shift Drive – Increased range], INARA.</ref>

{{#invoke:EngineeringBlueprints|infobox|fsd_increased_range}}

== Effects and trade-offs ==

The Blueprint scales through Grades 1–5. Higher grades progressively:

* increase optimized mass;
* increase the FSD's own mass;
* increase power draw; and
* reduce module integrity.

At Grade 5, the listed optimized-mass increase is 55%. The resulting jump range is not a fixed percentage because it also depends on the ship's total mass, FSD class and rating, fuel load, and other fitted equipment.

{{#invoke:EngineeringBlueprints|gradeTable|fsd_increased_range}}

== Selection considerations ==

Increased Range is the standard Blueprint choice when jump range is the main objective. It is useful on exploration ships, long-distance transports, and general-purpose vessels that benefit from fewer jumps between systems.

The increased module mass and power draw partially offset the range gain, while reduced integrity makes the drive less durable. Those penalties should be included in the complete ship build rather than assessing the optimized-mass modifier in isolation.

[[Faster Boot Sequence]] provides a smaller optimized-mass increase while prioritising FSD startup time. [[Shielded]] instead prioritises integrity and thermal behaviour. Compatible [[Experimental Effects|Experimental Effects]] can further adjust range, mass, heat, fuel use, or integrity, but only one Experimental Effect may be installed on the drive.

== Availability ==

{{#invoke:EngineeringBlueprints|engineers|fsd_increased_range}}

Blueprint grades can be applied through [[Remote Engineering]] after the Blueprint is pinned and the required Engineer access has been earned. Experimental Effects still require a visit to an Engineer workshop.
